items.title: Anthropic revealed enormous compute purchase commitments
items.oneliner: Anthropic disclosed $895.4 billion in commitments. Frontier AI is now constrained by power, chips, and contracts.

items.title: OpenAI is now managing grid stress
items.oneliner: OpenAI's 1GW Georgia demand-response program makes power scheduling a first-class part of AI deployment.

items.title: Qwen can inspect weights, not magically improve them
items.oneliner: Qwen 3.8 27B can read model weights, but the real gains still come from generated experiments and code.

items.title: DeepSeek turned prompts into plugin generation
items.oneliner: DeepSeek Harness now builds plugins from prompts, pushing agent tooling one step closer to real software assembly.

items.title: Postman crossed a dangerous trust boundary
items.oneliner: Postman allegedly auto-installed AI plugins and rewired configs silently. That is a supply-chain trust failure, not onboarding.

items.title: Google is pressuring schools on AI adoption
items.oneliner: Google may restrict search for schools rejecting AI, turning platform power into an adoption mandate.

items.title: Proton staff pushed back on AI mandates
items.oneliner: Proton reportedly canceled AI re-interviews after employee backlash, showing internal AI policy can become a retention risk.

items.title: AI demand is reviving magnetic tape
items.oneliner: Fujifilm is boosting tape production 5x. Cold storage is back because AI data growth is outrunning cheap disks.

items.title: ByteDance published a cheaper recommender storage stack
items.oneliner: ByteDance says USDB cut write latency 85.8% and infrastructure cost 42.1%, which matters more than another demo model.

items.title: Mac cloud infrastructure is getting improvised
items.oneliner: Namespace Labs racked MacBook Pros in a datacenter, a reminder that Apple bottlenecks still shape developer infrastructure.
